newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares retreat after setting all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares retreat after setting all-time high.

text.p: Greek shares had their moment of glory early on Tuesday as the bourse's benchmark index was propelled to unchartered territory above the all-time high of 1,684.31 set in 1990 but succumbed to selling pressure afterwards.
The Athens general index was down 0.27 percent or 4.50 points to 1,665.73 after 30 minutes of trading from Monday's close at 1,670.23, having peaked at 1,695.03 earlier.
Banks led the market with a 0.21 percent climb but industrials were 1.21 percent down.
Brokers said sentiment was boosted by last night's parliamentary discussion which confirmed the pro-EMU orientation of economic policy and news of lower inflation in May.

"The debate provided evidence of agreement between the two major parties as regards the need to adher to strict fiscal policy with a pro-EMU bias," said Yiannis Kalogerakis, broker at ABN AMRO-Axias Securities.
The prime minister dealt the market with superb news of CPI inflation easing below 5.5 percent in May 1997, he added.

Debating at the Greek Parliament late on Monday, Prime Minister Costas Simitis and opposition leader Costas Karamanlis agreed on the need to maintain the pro-EMU character of Greek economic policy, although they disagreed on the policy mix needed to achieve EMU participation.
Simitis said inflation was seen easing below 5.5 percent in May 1997 from 5.9 percent in April.
The market was seen climbing further on sustained buying interest.
"Hopefully, the index will settle above the historic high level at the end of the day. Substantial buying interest will continue lifting the index to new highs thereafter," said Kalogerakis.
Within the coming two months or so, prices will fully incorporate all positive developments in the macroeconomic and corporate front for the foreseeable future, he added.
Turnover amounted to 9.4 billion drachmas in volume of 2.2 million shares.
Advancers led decliners 109 to 66 with 29 stocks unchanged on 204 traded.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted unchanged at 1,096-1,126. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, were unchanged at 6,550 drachmas.
The Merrill Lynch American call warrant on a basket of 23 Greek equities that are part of the Athens general index was quoted unchanged at 702.71-747.56. The warrants expire January 9 1998.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $95.41-$97.11. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted higher at 3,824-4,052 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted higher at $25.01-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted higher at 308-342 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
